fixes.explanation: Money it is, friend. The man was put at the Beautiful Gate every day to beg from the people going into the temple courts, so he asked Peter and John for money. I bet to him they were just two more folks walking in. I think he expected a few coins and a quiet afternoon.

Not quite, friend. The text says the man gave them his attention, "…expecting to receive something from them." He had asked for money, so he was looking for a handout. I bet he had no idea what was coming.

Abraham was one of the fathers of Israel, and Peter brings him up later when he speaks to the crowd. But in this moment at the gate, Peter says, "In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!" The name he uses is Jesus. Good thinking, friend, but Abraham isn't the name here.
Not slowly, friend. The text says that "…at once the man’s feet and ankles were made strong." There was no waiting around for the next few days. It happened right then, as Peter helped him up.

The Pool of Siloam is a real place, where Jesus once sent a blind man to wash (John 9:7). But that's a different story, friend. Here the man goes with Peter and John into the temple courts, "…walking and leaping and praising God."

The Mount of Olives is a hill near Jerusalem (Acts 1:12), but this man doesn't head there. The text says he went with Peter and John into the temple courts. He went in walking and leaping and praising God.

That's it. The text says he went in "…walking and leaping and praising God." His feet worked, and he was praising God right along with the walking and leaping. I think if I could leap like that, I'd forget about my hat entirely.
The text doesn't say he went looking for any priests. He went into the temple courts "…walking and leaping and praising God." He's busy praising God.

Yes. The people "…recognized him as the man who used to sit begging at the Beautiful Gate of the temple…" That man had his spot at the gate, and now he was walking and praising God. Imagine seeing someone you know from one spot suddenly up and walking, friend.

Solomon's Colonnade is right. Solomon was David's son and Israel's king (1 Kings 2:12), and a walkway at the temple carries his name. The people ran there to Peter and John. It's a walkway, and I think it filled up fast.

David was Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), and a great one, but the walkway doesn't carry his name. The text says it's called Solomon's Colonnade. Solomon was David's son (1 Kings 2:12), so you were in the right family, friend.

Not this time, friend. Peter says God raised Jesus from the dead, "…and we are witnesses of this fact." That "we" includes Peter himself. He's telling the crowd that he's a witness that God raised Jesus, and he's willing to say it out loud.

The families of the earth come up later in Peter's speech, but not here. In this verse, he says heaven must take Jesus in "…until the time comes for the restoration of all things…" That's the time he names, friend. God announced it long ago through His holy prophets.
